newsitem.title: USA: NHL-PANTHERS REMAIN ONLY UNBEATEN TEAM WITH VICTORY OVER RANGERS.
newsitem.headline: NHL-PANTHERS REMAIN ONLY UNBEATEN TEAM WITH VICTORY OVER RANGERS.

text.p: Per Gustafsson had a goal and two assists as the unbeaten Florida Panthers scored a team-record five power-play goals on the way to a 6-4 win Friday over the New York Rangers.
The Panthers, the only unbeaten team in the National Hockey League, improved to 6-0-3 and increased their lead in the Atlantic Division to five points over Tampa Bay and Philadelphia.
"It's not something we set out to do," said Florida's Gord Murphy. "We never expected to have this kind of record considering the opposition that we've played."
After starting the season 1-for-30 on the power play in its first seven games, Florida is 8-for-14 in its last two.
"We like the look of the loss column," said Florida goalie John Vanbiesbrouck. "It puts a smile on our faces. The Rangers are a high-powered team and we beat them at their own game."

With New York's Bruce Driver serving a hooking penalty, Ray Sheppard passed from behind the net to Gustafsson, who fired a wrist shot past Mike Richter to give Florida a 2-1 lead just 34 seconds into the second period and the Panthers were on their way.
After the Panthers increased their lead to 4-1, Gustafsson corraled a loose puck at the left point and ripped a slap shot that was deflected past Richter by Dave Lowry at 5:18.

The Rangers (3-6-2) cut the deficit to 5-4 in a 5:40 span of the third period. Wayne Gretzky and Mark Messier had power-play goals before Messier scored New York's second shorthanded tally to draw within one goal with 4:10 left.

But the Rangers' inability to stay out of the penalty box cost them. Defenceman Eric Cairns was still in the box serving a cross-checking penalty when Gustafsson fed Scott Mellanby behind the net. Mellanby found Robert Svehla alone in the slot and he buried a wrister past Mike Richter to cap the scoring.
The goal came 18 seconds after Messier's tally.
"We're frustrated and disappointed by the whole situation," said Gretzky. "We're playing in desperation."
In Detroit, Brendan Shanahan's goal with 4:55 left in the second period lifted the Detroit Red Wings into a 2-2 tie with the Chicago Blackhawks.
Shanahan flipped the puck past goaltender Jimmy Waite from the low slot off a rebound of Steve Yzerman's shot for his fifth goal in three games.
Waite, recalled after playing Thursday for Indianapolis of the International Hockey League, made 39 saves for Chicago.
Detroit (5-4-1) started third-stringer Kevin Hodson, who made 26 saves and helped the Wings extend their unbeaten streak to four games (3-0-1).
Chicago (6-3-1), unbeaten in their last five games (4-0-1), grabbed a 2-0 lead in the first period on power-play goals by Gary Suter and Eric Daze.
The first period was fight-filled as referee Paul Stewart handed out 50 minutes in penalties.
The Red Wings got on the board 2:28 into the second when Vyacheslav Kozlov put a bad-angle shot through Waite's pads after skating down the left wing.
